boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented RPI customs and rituals, including several preserved as historical traditions by the Institute Archives.

cards.title: Big Red Freakout
cards.subtitle: RPI hockey spirit event
cards.notes: Attend an announced Freakout game in red, follow arena staff directions, and join the crowd’s approved cheering without bringing prohibited noisemakers.
cards.short_summary: An annual RPI hockey tradition built around a designated high-energy game.
cards.evidence_claim: RPI’s Institute Archives says the first Big Red Freakout in 1978 asked fans to wear red, make banners, stay for skating, and make noise.
cards.source_title: Big Red Freakout #1 | Institute Archives and Special Collections
cards.access_notes: Check RPI Athletics for the current game, ticket, and arena-entry details.

cards.title: Grand Marshal Week
cards.subtitle: Student-election tradition
cards.notes: Watch for officially announced student-government election events and campaign information; engage through the current election process rather than reenacting historic festivities.
cards.short_summary: A long-running campus election period associated with the Grand Marshal office.
cards.evidence_claim: The Institute Archives documents Grand Marshal Week activity in the 1870s and notes campus campaigning before the 2008 election.
cards.source_title: Grand Marshal Week, 1870s | Institute Archives and Special Collections
cards.access_notes: Use official RPI student-government announcements for any current events or voting procedures.

cards.title: The Grand Marshal’s Silk Top Hat
cards.subtitle: Historic student-leadership symbol
cards.notes: See archival material about the Grand Marshal office and its ceremonial top hat; treat it as a documented symbol, not an invitation to handle institutional artifacts.
cards.short_summary: A silk top hat historically awarded to RPI’s elected Grand Marshal.
cards.evidence_claim: The Institute Archives reports that a silk top hat was awarded to the Grand Marshal in 1876 and says the tradition predates that year.
cards.source_title: Grand Marshal Week, 1870s | Institute Archives and Special Collections
cards.access_notes: Historical artifact tradition; consult the Institute Archives for collection access.

cards.entity_name: Grand Marshal and President of the Union Election
cards.title: The GM and PU Election
cards.subtitle: RPI’s paired student offices
cards.notes: Learn how the two historic student offices are recorded, then use current Student Government channels for active-election information and participation rules.
cards.short_summary: The Institute Archives preserves a historical list of RPI’s Grand Marshals and Presidents of the Union.
cards.evidence_claim: RPI’s Archives states that the Grand Marshal and President of the Union were traditionally elected during the spring semester.
cards.source_title: Grand Marshal and President of Union - Historical List | Institute Archives and Special Collections
cards.access_notes: Historical record; current election timing and eligibility should be confirmed with RPI Student Government.

cards.title: The 'Tute Screw
cards.subtitle: Historic freshman-class trophy
cards.notes: Read the archive’s account of this unusual trophy tradition and keep the visit interpretive: the source documents its origin rather than a current participatory event.
cards.short_summary: A historic RPI object whose first presentation was tied to the freshman class.
cards.evidence_claim: The Institute Archives says the first 'Tute Screw was awarded in fall 1949, when the Order of the Royal Screw presented the trophy to the freshman class.
cards.source_title: RPI History Revealed | Institute Archives and Special Collections
cards.access_notes: Historical tradition; availability of any artifact for viewing is not stated.

cards.title: Cheery Pi
cards.subtitle: Mathematical RPI cheer
cards.notes: Explore the archive’s transcription of this math-heavy cheer as RPI history; use official event guidance before joining any present-day athletic cheering.
cards.short_summary: An archival RPI cheer mixing calculus language with digits of pi.
cards.evidence_claim: The Institute Archives identifies Cheery Pi as a cheer that included mathematical language and digits of pi.
cards.source_title: RPI History Revealed | Institute Archives and Special Collections
cards.access_notes: Historical documentation; no current performance schedule is stated.

cards.title: GM Week Egg Drop
cards.subtitle: Engineering-style survival challenge
cards.notes: If a current organizer announces an egg drop, participate only under its published safety rules; otherwise use the archive to trace the contest’s documented history.
cards.short_summary: A GM Week contest in which participants designed containers intended to protect an egg during a drop.
cards.evidence_claim: An Institute Archives post records alumni and staff descriptions of an Egg Drop Contest held during GM Week, including containers designed to keep eggs intact.
cards.source_title: Falling Objects | Institute Archives and Special Collections
cards.access_notes: Historical account; do not conduct drops outside an officially supervised event.

cards.title: The Hockey Line
cards.subtitle: Historic season-ticket queue
cards.notes: Read the Archives’ history of the hockey-ticket queue and use current RPI Athletics sales procedures instead of attempting to recreate extended line-waiting.
cards.short_summary: A long-standing RPI tradition associated with student hockey season-ticket sales.
cards.evidence_claim: The Institute Archives calls the Hockey Line a long-standing RPI tradition and traces its development from early-1970s ticket sales.
cards.source_title: At the Beginning of the Hockey Line | Institute Archives and Special Collections
cards.access_notes: Historical tradition; follow current ticketing rules and do not camp or queue outside authorized procedures.

cards.title: Winter Carnival
cards.subtitle: Recurring winter festivities
cards.notes: Look for an officially scheduled Winter Carnival, then choose advertised activities and weather-appropriate clothing; the archive records several earlier versions of the event.
cards.short_summary: An RPI winter-event tradition with snow sculptures and other seasonal activities in its history.
cards.evidence_claim: The Institute Archives documents Winter Weekend/Carnival events at RPI, including snow sculpture contests, and notes a 2009 return of Winter Carnival.
cards.source_title: Winter Carnival | Institute Archives and Special Collections
cards.access_notes: Historical continuity varies; verify whether a current event is scheduled before planning a visit.

cards.title: Reunion & Homecoming
cards.subtitle: Annual alumni return to campus
cards.notes: If you are eligible to attend, consult the official alumni calendar for the current program and registration details; the Archives characterizes the gathering as annual.
cards.short_summary: An annual campus return tradition for RPI alumni and their families.
cards.evidence_claim: The Institute Archives describes Reunion & Homecoming as an annual ritual in which alumni and families gather on campus.
cards.source_title: Yearly Archive 2013 | Institute Archives and Special Collections
cards.access_notes: Confirm current event dates, eligibility, and registration through RPI Alumni Relations.
